We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to be the primary product voice for Elastic Security's most strategic enterprise customers. Solid products are built on a clear knowledge of real customer needs. In large enterprise accounts, those needs arrive as a constant stream of enhancement requests, feature asks, and hard problems.

They often arrive faster than any one team can act on them. Someone has to bring order to that stream, tell apart what a customer wants from what a customer needs, and turn it into a coherent product direction across different product areas.
In this high-impact role, you will own the relationship between Elastic Security's product organization and our most strategic enterprise accounts. You will manage enhancement requests across many enterprise customers at once.

You will prioritize them with judgment and data, and make sure they keep transitioning through the system instead of sitting idle.

You will be the person a CISO trusts in the room, the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and the person who can tell a major customer that something will not be built without losing the relationship.

You will work at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Engineering, building the structure that lets Elastic scale close customer relationships without simply adding headcount.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the enhancement request pipeline across multiple strategic enterprise accounts at once. Build and maintain a structured system to track, prioritize, and respond to customer-sourced requirements, and keep requests moving rather than leaving them in “under consideration.”
Translate customer requirements into shipped products. Work at the level of customer pain, not just the feature that was asked for, and synthesize input from many accounts into a single, coherent product direction.
Turn input from strategic accounts into successful products. Look for patterns across accounts. Shape some of these patterns into formal partnerships for design. Make sure the resulting capabilities benefit the wider market, not just the single customer that made the request.
Feed validated customer patterns back into the core product roadmaps, influencing direction well beyond the accounts you cover.
Serve as the primary product voice in meetings with senior customer stakeholders, including the CISO, CTO, and VP of Security Operations. Deliver roadmap updates, including deprioritizations and misses, in a way that keeps the relationship deep.
Prioritize customer-sourced requirements using structured frameworks such as RICE, weighted scoring, and opportunity sizing. Use data where it is available and clear judgment where it is thin, and be transparent about which is which.
Partner with product and engineering leads to write requirements they can act on without follow-up clarification meetings. Understand system architecture well enough to assess feasibility and scope on your own.
Operate across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Legal. Support deal cycles as a product resource through RFP responses, security questionnaires, and roadmap presentations to prospects.
Navigate tension between a customer's contractual expectations and the internal roadmap , and tackle it directly rather than through routine escalation.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers, enhancement request dashboards, and decision memos that give customers and internal stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.
Advocate for customer needs inside the company while resisting the pull of the loudest or largest customer setting the roadmap at the expense of the broader market.

Extensive Experience: 7–10 years of product management experience, with at least 4 years in B2B enterprise software. A consistent record of owning a product area with meaningful revenue impact and of leading products from customer input through shipped, iterated outcomes. Direct experience working with named strategic accounts, not only through customer success proxies. Experience with hyperscalers, MSSPs and/or PubSec is a solid plus.
Security Domain Knowledge: Hands-on knowledge with SIEM, SOAR, XDR or broader security operations platforms, either as a product manager or as a practitioner such as a SOC analyst, detection engineer, or security architect.

You can credibly discuss detection engineering, log ingestion pipelines, correlation rules, threat hunting workflows, and compliance use cases without a solutions engineer in the room. You understand the difference between what a CISO wants to hear and what a SOC analyst actually needs.

A background as a security practitioner, such as SOC, incident response, or detection engineering, before moving into product is a solid plus, and brings credibility that is hard to teach.
Enhancement Request Management at Scale: You have personally run a structured enhancement request pipeline across several enterprise accounts at the same time. You can step into a relationship with dozens of open requests and no prior documentation and build a working tracking system within weeks.
Executive Presence: You are comfortable as the primary product voice with C-suite and VP-level customer stakeholders. You can deliver difficult news without losing the relationship, and you can hold both the executive view and the analyst view in the same meeting.
Technical Credibility: You earn respect from engineering through the quality of your requirements rather than through authority. You write specs engineers can act on, and you know enough about architecture to judge feasibility and scope.
Cross-functional Leadership and Influence: You have operated at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, and Legal, and you know which function owns what and how to advance work across all of them. You lead across a matrixed organization, align multiple stakeholders toward a common vision, and drive execution in a dynamic, remote-first environment, with the autonomy and judgment expected of a principal-level product leader.
Structured Thinking and Bias for Closure: You bring order to unstructured problems, using data to prioritize and clear judgment when data is thin, and staying transparent about which is which. You move work through the system and follow up proactively rather than waiting to be asked, defaulting to visibility through artifacts instead of meetings. You advocate for customer needs while synthesizing them into product direction rather than relaying demands.

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the core marketplace experience. We’re rethinking things from the ground up—you won’t be inheriting a roadmap, a backlog, or a set of conventions. You’ll be building the product from the ground up alongside the CPTO.
This role requires someone who thinks in systems. A marketplace is not a single product—it’s an ecosystem. You’ll need to hold the consumer experience, the practitioner experience, the matching logic, the trust and safety layer, the business model, and the growth loops in your head simultaneously, and make smart tradeoffs between them every day.
You will report directly to the CPTO and work alongside a small, senior engineering team. There are no layers between you and the work, and no layers between you and the decisions that shape the company.

Product Strategy & Vision
Define the product vision and strategy for the marketplace, grounded in deep user understanding, competitive analysis, and a clear-eyed view of the business model.
Own the roadmap end-to-end. Decide what to build, what to kill, and what to sequence—with conviction, not consensus.
Develop and maintain a strong point of view on where the wellness and longevity market is heading and how our product should evolve to lead, not follow.
TRUE 0→1 product thinking: identify the fastest and cheapest ways to validate core assumptions before committing significant engineering investment.
Marketplace Systems Thinking
Design and optimize both sides of the marketplace: the consumer journey (discovery → trust → booking → retention) and the practitioner journey (onboarding → activation → growth → advocacy).
Develop frameworks for marketplace health: supply/demand balance, liquidity metrics, matching quality, and network effects.
Own the cold-start playbook. Figure out how to bootstrap supply and demand in new verticals and geographies.
Think critically about marketplace trust and safety—credential verification, reviews, dispute resolution—as a product surface, not an afterthought.
Execution & Shipping
Partner with engineering and design to ship continuously. Write clear, opinionated specs. Run structured discovery. Make scope decisions that keep velocity high.
Instrument everything. Define success metrics for every feature. Run experiments. Kill things that aren’t working.
Balance competing priorities across consumer, practitioner, and platform workstreams while maintaining a clear view of the overall system.
Business & Growth
Own the business logic of the marketplace: pricing models, take rates, subscription tiers, transaction economics.
Partner with growth and marketing on acquisition loops, activation funnels, and retention strategies for both sides of the marketplace.
Use data to identify the highest-leverage opportunities. Build the instrumentation and dashboards needed to operate with clarity.
AI as a Force Multiplier
AI should be part of your daily operating system as a product manager.
Research synthesis: distilling user interviews, market data, and competitive intel at speed.
Spec and strategy drafting: using AI to accelerate writing, then applying your judgment to sharpen it.
Data analysis: querying, visualizing, and interpreting data with AI assistance.
Prototyping: rapidly generating UI concepts, user flows, and copy variations.
Workflow automation: building personal and team workflows that eliminate toil.
Bring a perspective on how AI should be woven into the product itself—personalized recommendations, intelligent matching, automated practitioner tools.
Raise the AI fluency bar for the entire team. Share what’s working. Push others to adopt.

Experience & Background
7+ years of product management experience, with significant time on marketplace, platform, or multi-sided products.
You’ve been a startup founder, a founding PM, or an early employee who built 0→1 products with limited resources. You know what it’s like to ship when there’s no playbook, no established process, and no safety net.
You’ve operated at the Senior, Staff, or Principal level—or you’ve functioned at that altitude regardless of your title (common for founders and early-stage operators).
Proven ability to ship products that drive measurable business outcomes, not just features.
Domain Passion
You are passionate about wellness, longevity, and preventive health. This isn’t a box you’re checking—you have a personal connection to this space. Maybe you’ve seen the healthcare system fail someone you love. Maybe you’ve gone deep on your own health optimization. Maybe you’ve worked in healthtech and know firsthand how much better it could be.
You stay current on trends in functional medicine, longevity research, consumer health, and the evolving practitioner landscape.
Working Style
Exceptional product taste. You see what’s working, what’s not, and what’s missing—and you care about the details.
Clear, precise communicator—in writing, in specs, in conversation, and in a room with engineers.
Comfortable with ambiguity and pace. You don’t need permission to act. You don’t wait for perfect information.
Strong analytical chops. You pull your own data, run your own analyses, and let evidence shape your decisions.
Low ego, high ownership. You do what needs to be done—whether that’s writing a spec, responding to a user complaint, or fixing a broken onboarding email.

Direct experience in health, wellness, longevity, or consumer health—and an understanding of the regulatory, trust, and compliance dynamics of the space.
Experience building or scaling a marketplace through cold-start, supply/demand balancing, and network effects.
Experience building AI-native products (not just AI features bolted onto existing workflows).
Technical depth—you can read code, write SQL, or prototype in no-code/low-code tools.

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser, and Pocket, a service for keeping up with the best content online.

And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.
The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders - only to our mission. Query understanding, Autosuggestions and AI/ML problems in the Search domain
Where conversational and agentic search changes how customers get to a decision.
Making search work across three brands, multiple languages, and query behaviour that differs market by market.

You demonstrate fluency with search measurement and know how to actually move it.
You show strong product judgment, backed by data literacy and customer insight.

You're comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely flexible. This industry is changing fast, AI most of all, and the plan we write in January won't be the plan in June.

You're curious about what AI actually changes for customers, and you can tell real value from hype.
You build a case and bring people with you: engineering, design, analytics, and local market teams across three brands and many markets.
You do your best work with range: global platform thinking one week, a specific market's reality the next.

We are a 100% remote company with 1,600+ team members across 40+ countries, and we’re backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .
We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK.

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals.

You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.
Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

As the Staff Product Manager for OpenTelemetry Experience, you’ll own the end-to-end journey for helping people and agents instrument workloads and successfully send useful OpenTelemetry data to Grafana Cloud.
Your mission is to make Grafana Cloud the easiest and most trusted destination for OpenTelemetry workloads. You’ll reduce the uncertainty, complexity, and failure points users encounter between deciding to adopt OpenTelemetry and receiving healthy, correctly attributed, and actionable telemetry in Grafana Cloud.
Teams can instrument workloads, directly or with the help of coding agents, through OpenTelemetry SDKs, automatic instrumentation technologies such as Beyla and SDK injection, or client-side OpenTelemetry Collectors. Each path presents different decisions, deployment requirements, configuration steps, and potential failure modes.

You’ll define a coherent experience that helps users choose the right approach, complete setup successfully, troubleshoot problems, and understand whether their telemetry is healthy and useful. You’ll design a future in which a growing share of instrumentation work is performed by coding agents acting on behalf of developers.

This means treating agents are first-class participants in the experience and ensuring that instrumentation options, configuration requirements, errors, and validation signals are structured, discoverable, and actionable by both humans and machines.

OpenTelemetry SDK onboarding and configuration
Automatic instrumentation experiences, including OBI/Beyla and SDK injection
Client-side OpenTelemetry Collector deployment and onboarding
Collector configuration, authentication, and initial connectivity
Guidance and machine-readable context that help people and agents choose the right instrumentation approach
Workflows that allow coding-agents to implement, configure and verify instrumentation safely
Troubleshooting missing, incomplete, malformed, or unhealthy telemetry
Validation signals that allow both people and agents to confirm that telemetry is healthy, correctly attributed, and usable in Grafana Cloud
The transition from receiving telemetry to activating the appropriate Grafana Cloud observability solution
Success does not stop when Grafana Cloud receives the first data point. Telemetry must arrive with the quality, context, and structure required to support meaningful observability outcomes. You’ll partner closely with teams responsible for experiences such as Application Observability, Kubernetes Monitoring, Infrastructure Observability, and Drilldown Apps to ensure OpenTelemetry workloads receive a first-class experience from initial setup through first value.
This is a horizontal Staff-level product leadership role spanning multiple products and engineering teams. You may not directly own every SDK, collector, instrumentation technology, or downstream application involved in the journey. You will, however, be accountable for the coherence of the overall customer experience, its success measures, and the cross-product strategy required to improve it.
AI will also be part of how you work, not only what you build. You’ll be expected to use AI tools regularly to accelerate customer-research synthesis, analyze product signals, explore technical workflows, prototype experiences, develop positioning content, and test agent-led instrumentation journeys. You’ll model thoughtful, hands-on adoption of AI while applying strong judgement to its outputs.
The role is not focused on developing OpenTelemetry as an open source project in isolation. You’ll engage with and contribute to the OpenTelemetry ecosystem where appropriate, while measuring success through customer activation and outcomes in Grafana Cloud.

Define the vision, strategy, and cross-product roadmap for the journey from an uninstrumented workload to healthy, useful telemetry in Grafana Cloud solutions
Create coherent, opinionated experiences that help users choose and implement the right approach across SDK instrumentation, automatic instrumentation, and Collector-based deployment while preserving the flexibility advanced users require
Identify and eliminate the leading causes of setup failure, abandonment, misconfiguration, and low-quality telemetry
Establish shared experience principles, priorities, and success criteria across the product and engineering teams contributing to the OpenTelemetry journey
Use customer research, product data, and market insight to prioritize investments and measure outcomes such as onboarding completion, time to useful telemetry, telemetry health, and workload expansion
Partner with downstream Grafana Cloud solution teams to create a coherent transition from telemetry ingestion to meaningful product activation

At Too Good To Go, we dream of a planet with no food waste.
Did you know that more than 40% of all food produced gets thrown away? This unnecessary food waste — and the resources needed to produce and transport it — accounts for 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
Too Good To Go is a certified B Corporation on a mission to end food waste. We connect stores with surplus food to consumers across 20 markets in Europe, North America, and APAC — with over 140 million registered users, more than 200,000 daily active stores, and 600 million meals saved from going to waste.
Why This Role
Pricing sits at the centre of everything we do. It shapes what partners earn, what consumers pay, and how much surplus food actually gets saved. Today, pricing decisions are made in different places, for different reasons, without a single team owning the strategy end to end.
We are changing that. We are building our first dedicated Pricing team — and you will be the founding member.
You will start with a concrete, high-value problem: the pricing infrastructure behind our Key Account deals. That's your launchpad — from there, you will have real scope to shape our approach to dynamic pricing, consumer-facing service fees, and pricing strategy across Too Good To Go more broadly. This is a role built for someone who wants to define a domain, not just execute a brief.
The goal behind everything we do is twofold: save as much surplus food as possible, and grow the pie between TGTG, our Partners, and our Consumers — never trading one off against the other.
There is a further dimension to this. We are expanding beyond food into new non-food, non-perishable categories — and that growth brings pricing complexity and opportunity we have not had to solve before. Getting ahead of that, rather than reacting to it, is part of this role.

As Senior Product Manager for Pricing, you will build the foundation for how Too Good To Go prices its marketplace — starting with Key Account deals, then extending across the business.
In the near term, you will design and ship the infrastructure that lets us set, manage, and evolve pricing for Key Account partnerships with the flexibility our commercial teams need.

From there, you will develop a smarter, more dynamic pricing algorithm that responds to supply, demand, and partner economics — replacing static rules with something genuinely intelligent. Alongside this, you will investigate our consumer-facing service fees: how they're structured, how they're perceived, and where there is room to optimise.
Underneath all of it are two questions you will own: how do we price in a way that saves as much surplus food as possible, and how do we grow the pie for everyone — Too Good To Go, our Partners, and our Consumers — rather than shifting value from one side to another? Answering both well means understanding marketplace pricing broadly: the best practices and patterns other two- and three-sided marketplaces use, and what applies to ours.
Pricing decisions rarely stay inside one product's boundaries, so you will work across product teams and the wider organisation — Commercial, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, and Key Accounts — to make sure pricing is right everywhere it shows up, not just within your own roadmap. You will become the go-to person for anything pricing-related at Too Good To Go, including presenting your strategy and results to the Global Management Team.
You will also help lay the pricing groundwork for our move into non-food, non-perishable categories — different cost structures, margins, and purchase patterns than the food pricing we know today, and a chance to shape pricing thinking for a new part of the business from the start.

You will be the founding Pricing PM, operating as an individual contributor, with a small dedicated engineering team of around 3-4 developers to start. We will grow the team's scope and headcount as we prove impact, not before. You will report directly to our VP of Product.
This is a new team with a clear starting point, not a fixed script. You will know where to begin — Key Account deals — but how the team's remit, roadmap, and impact grow from there is largely yours to shape. If you want a role where everything is already solved and you are just executing, this isn't it. If you want to help define what great pricing looks like across Too Good To Go, it is.
The role is suited to someone who does not need daily direction — who can set the agenda within that mandate, manage up effectively, and make strong pricing calls with incomplete information.

Build the pricing infrastructure for Key Account deals, giving commercial teams the tools and flexibility to structure partnerships well while keeping pricing logic sound and scalable.
Design and develop a smart pricing algorithm — moving from static, rules-based pricing toward a dynamic model informed by supply, demand, and partner-specific economics.
Investigate consumer-facing service fees: how they're set, how they perform, and how they should evolve to balance consumer value with business sustainability.
Take a holistic view of pricing across TGTG, Partners, and Consumers — optimising for meals saved and for growing the pie for all three, rather than trading one off against another.
Research and apply best practices and patterns from marketplace pricing more broadly, adapting proven approaches to our specific dynamics rather than reinventing from scratch.
Own the roadmap and OKRs for the Pricing team within its agreed mandate, sequencing the work so that early wins on Key Accounts build toward the algorithm and fee strategy.
Work across product teams and the wider organisation — Commercial, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, and Key Accounts — to make sure pricing decisions are right wherever they show up, not just within your own roadmap.
Be the go-to person for anything pricing-related at Too Good To Go, including presenting strategy, models, and results to the Global Management Team.

Use data rigorously — pricing experiments, elasticity analysis, partner and consumer feedback — to test hypotheses before scaling them.

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals.

You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.
Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

As the Staff Product Manager for OpenTelemetry Experience, you’ll own the end-to-end journey for helping people and agents instrument workloads and successfully send useful OpenTelemetry data to Grafana Cloud.
Your mission is to make Grafana Cloud the easiest and most trusted destination for OpenTelemetry workloads. You’ll reduce the uncertainty, complexity, and failure points users encounter between deciding to adopt OpenTelemetry and receiving healthy, correctly attributed, and actionable telemetry in Grafana Cloud.
Teams can instrument workloads, directly or with the help of coding agents, through OpenTelemetry SDKs, automatic instrumentation technologies such as Beyla and SDK injection, or client-side OpenTelemetry Collectors. Each path presents different decisions, deployment requirements, configuration steps, and potential failure modes.

You’ll define a coherent experience that helps users choose the right approach, complete setup successfully, troubleshoot problems, and understand whether their telemetry is healthy and useful. You’ll design a future in which a growing share of instrumentation work is performed by coding agents acting on behalf of developers.

This means treating agents are first-class participants in the experience and ensuring that instrumentation options, configuration requirements, errors, and validation signals are structured, discoverable, and actionable by both humans and machines.

OpenTelemetry SDK onboarding and configuration
Automatic instrumentation experiences, including OBI/Beyla and SDK injection
Client-side OpenTelemetry Collector deployment and onboarding
Collector configuration, authentication, and initial connectivity
Guidance and machine-readable context that help people and agents choose the right instrumentation approach

MongoDB is seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Senior Product Manager to own the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of Revenue and Order to Cash (OTC) capabilities that enable accurate, scalable, and efficient revenue operations.
This role will work closely with the Group Product Manager, Quote to Cash (QTC), owning the OTC and revenue processes within the broader QTC organization, while partnering across Finance, Revenue Operations, Sales, Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, and Program Management to improve the end-to-end order-to-cash lifecycle — order management through billing, collections, revenue recognition, and close — and help the business scale with reliable, increasingly automated revenue systems.
You will own product discovery, prioritization, requirements, delivery partnership, and launch readiness across the OTC and revenue lifecycle — including order management, subscription and contract operations, billing, accounts receivable, collections, renewals, revenue recognition, month-end and quarter-end close, and ERP integrations.

The central focus of this role is revenue accuracy and timeliness: reducing manual adjustments, strengthening SOX and audit controls, accelerating time to invoice and cash, and building a foundation for continuous process improvement across the revenue lifecycle.

Define and maintain the Revenue/OTC product vision, strategy, roadmap, and release priorities in alignment with company objectives, with revenue accuracy and close efficiency as the north star
Partner closely with the Group Product Manager, QTC to align the OTC and revenue roadmap with the broader Quote to Cash strategy, while owning the order-to-cash and revenue processes as your dedicated area of focus
Build deep expertise in NetSuite and the surrounding revenue systems landscape, including billing, accounts receivable, revenue recognition, month-end and quarter-end close, order management, contract and subscription data, ERP integrations, and related Finance and GTM systems
Elicit, analyze, and document business and functional requirements across the OTC lifecycle; translate them into clear epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and an actionable product backlog
Lead prioritization across competing Finance, Revenue Operations, and Sales needs, balancing near-term business value with long-term scalability and architectural health of revenue systems
Partner with Stakeholders, Lead PdM, Engineering, Architecture, TPM/Program Management, and implementation partners to evaluate and integrate strategic first- and third-party solutions for OTC and revenue processes
Define success metrics and KPIs for Revenue/OTC initiatives — such as billing accuracy, days sales outstanding (DSO), manual journal entry volume, and close cycle time — using data and stakeholder feedback to validate assumptions and measure post-launch outcomes
Own and improve end-to-end revenue workflows across order capture, billing, accounts receivable, collections, renewals, revenue recognition, month-end/quarter-end close, and reporting, including support for subscription and consumption-based business models
Provide product oversight for revenue controls, data definitions, business logic, integrations, and the overall consistency of the user experience across OTC systems
Coordinate integrated, cross-functional testing and partner with technology and business leads on release strategy, change management, training, and adoption for revenue system changes
Identify opportunities to improve revenue accuracy, accelerate time to invoice and cash, reduce billing leakage and manual journal entries, strengthen auditability and SOX compliance, simplify close processes, and maximize the return on investment of Revenue/OTC products
Communicate product decisions, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and progress clearly to stakeholders and executive audiences, with particular fluency in revenue and close-related metrics

Required Experience and Skills
8+ years of relevant product management experience, with a proven track record of delivering enterprise business systems and influencing stakeholders at all levels
Strong experience with Order to Cash (OTC), Quote to Cash, or adjacent revenue and finance processes, with a clear emphasis on the order-to-cash and revenue recognition side of the lifecycle
Hands-on understanding of NetSuite-based billing and revenue operations, revenue recognition, accounts receivable, collections, month-end and quarter-end close, order management, subscription and contract data, and ERP or downstream revenue integrations
Strong NetSuite product and integration experience, with a solid understanding of Finance operations, revenue accounting, billing controls, SOX/audit requirements, and the upstream GTM processes that drive downstream revenue outcomes
Experience working with Agile/Scrum delivery teams as a Product Owner or equivalent product leader
Strong data analysis and metrics skills, including the ability to define revenue and close-related KPIs (e.g., DSO, billing accuracy, close cycle time) and use quantitative and qualitative inputs to drive prioritization
Experience managing complex integrations, data models, business rules, and dependencies across enterprise revenue platforms
Demonstrated success collaborating across Finance, Revenue Operations, Sales, Engineering, Architecture, and other cross-functional teams
Experience with consumption-based, subscription, or other complex commercial business models is a plus
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree is a plus
Personal Attributes
Strategic thinker who can connect revenue systems decisions to business and financial outcomes
Detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable managing multiple priorities and dependencies across the OTC lifecycle
Strong communicator who can make complex technical, financial, and operational topics clear to varied audiences
Effective decision-maker and problem solver who brings structure to ambiguity, especially around revenue controls and close processes
Self-motivated, adaptable, collaborative, and able to influence without direct authority
Customer- and stakeholder-focused, with a strong bias toward measurable revenue outcomes and continuous improvement
Why This Role Matters
Order to Cash is a critical business capability connecting commercial execution to accurate billing, cash collection, revenue recognition, and financial reporting. In this role, you will help make the revenue lifecycle a scalable business enabler by improving revenue integrity, strengthening NetSuite and related system foundations, accelerating cash realization, tightening SOX and audit controls, and reducing operational effort and risk across the OTC and close process.

The squad sits in Payments, but partners deeply with Finance teams to build the systems, abstractions and capabilities Monzo needs to operate safely, scale efficiently, and expand into new markets.

You’ll work on foundational financial infrastructure: the ledgers, data, controls, reporting, reconciliation and platform capabilities that help Monzo understand, account for and manage money across the bank.
This is a role for someone who gets genuinely excited by complex, technical infrastructure. The work is often behind the scenes, but it’s business-critical: it helps Monzo scale, launch new products and markets, support Finance, and keep the bank running safely.
🔑You’ll play a key role by...
Defining the product strategy and roadmap for Finance Infrastructure within Payments Platform.
Partnering closely with Engineering, Finance and Payments leaders to understand what Monzo needs from its financial systems today and as we scale.
Moving the team from reactive delivery towards a more strategic, product-led approach, asking why we’re building things, what good looks like, and how today’s choices support Monzo’s long-term needs.
Translating complex finance, accounting, operational and regulatory needs into scalable platform capabilities.
Prioritising across competing stakeholder needs, balancing urgent delivery with long-term system health.
Helping Monzo build financial infrastructure that can support multiple products, entities, countries, currencies and regulatory environments.
Building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across Finance, Engineering, Product and Operations.
Bringing strong product discipline, technical curiosity and systems thinking to a space that is critical to Monzo’s future growth.
🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…
You’re a strong senior Product Manager with experience owning complex technical, platform, infrastructure or financial systems.
You have enough technical depth to partner credibly with engineers and reason about systems, trade-offs, dependencies and long-term architecture.
You’re excited by “boring but critical” infrastructure, things like ledgers, reconciliation, financial data, controls, reporting, internal platforms, abstractions or backend systems.
You can work with senior and cross-functional stakeholders, including Finance, Engineering, Product and operational teams.
You’re comfortable bringing product thinking into ambiguous or stakeholder-heavy environments, and moving teams from request-led delivery towards long-term strategy.
You’re high-agency, ambitious and excited to stretch yourself in a team with a high bar.
You care about customers and business outcomes, even when the work is several layers removed from the end customer experience.
Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! Studies show that women and people of colour might hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. At Monzo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming team. If you’re passionate about this role and keen to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply— even if you don’t have everything that's listed just yet. Drop us your application, we’d love to hear from you!
🙌 What’s in it for you
💰 £125,000 - £145,000 ➕ Incentive Awards tied to your performance ➕ equity
✈️ We’ll help you relocate to the UK.
✅ We can sponsor your visa.
📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London)
⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.
📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.
🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup.

## Dein neuer Job ##
* In enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Product Manager Verantwortung für die stringente Planung, Umsetzung und kontinuierliche Verbesserung daten- sowie KI-basierter Lösungen übernehmen
* Aktive Mitgestaltung der konzernweiten Daten- und KI-Plattform und Sicherstellung eines stabilen, sicheren sowie effizienten Betriebs

* In einer modernen, zukunftsorientierten Bank mit viel Tradition spannende Wege finden, um den Konzern mitzugestalten

**Unser Development-Bereich betreut das Herzstück von Finnova - unsere Kernbankensoftware. In der Abteilung «Core & Regulations» suchen wir für das agile Scrum-Team «Gebühren, Tarife und Geldwäscherei» eine engagierte Persönlichkeit als Product Owner.

In dieser Schlüsselrolle übernimmst du Verantwortung für ein zentrales Produkt und gestaltest dessen Weiterentwicklung gemeinsam mit unserem Product Management sowie einem interdisziplinären Scrum-Team aktiv mit.

Dabei bringst du neue Ideen ein, setzt Impulse für kundenorientierte Lösungen und trägst dazu bei, unsere Kernbankensoftware fit für die Zukunft zu machen.**
## Du begeisterst dich für... ##
* die aktive Weiterentwicklung und die kontinuierliche Optimierung unseres Core-Banking-Produkts, um gemeinsam mit dem Produktteam die Produktstrategie erfolgreich umzusetzen und das Produkt auf das nächste Level zu heben
* die fachliche Führung eines crossfunktionalen Scrum-Teams nach agilen Prinzipien und die Förderung einer Kultur der Eigenverantwortung
* die Erfüllung der hohen Ansprüche unserer Finnova-Banken hinsichtlich Qualität, Stabilität, Sicherheit und Skalierbarkeit
* die enge Zusammenarbeit mit internen und externen Stakeholdern, um fachliche Anforderungen zu verstehen und in hochwertige Lösungen zu überführen
* die Pflege, Priorisierung des Product Backlogs, um den Kundennutzen und die Wertschöpfung der Produktentwicklung zu maximieren
* die Sicherstellung qualitativ hochwertiger und termingerechter Auslieferungen im Einklang mit der Product Roadmap
## Du begeisterst uns... ##
* mit einer abgeschlossenen höheren Ausbildung in Wirtschaftsinformatik, Banking & Finance oder einer vergleichbaren Qualifikation mit mehrjähriger Berufserfahrung und fundiertem bankfachlichem Know-how
* mit deinem ausgeprägten Fachwissen im Core Banking, insbesondere in den Bereichen Gebühren, Tarife und Geldwäscherei
* mit deiner nachweisbaren Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Senior Business Analyst in agilen Softwareentwicklungsprojekten
* mit deiner starken Kommunikationsfähigkeit im Umgang mit unterschiedlichsten Stakeholdern, von Kunden und Fachbereichen bis hin zu Softwareentwicklern
* mit deinem Gespür für Priorisierung sowie deinem konsequenten Fokus auf maximalen Kundennutzen
* mit deiner analytischen und konzeptionellen Arbeitsweise sowie mit deiner innovativen und teamorientierten Persönlichkeit
* mit verhandlungssicheren Deutsch- und Englischkenntnissen
**Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft des Bankings! Bereit, Verantwortung zu übernehmen? Dann freuen wir uns, dich kennenzulernen.**

## Tâches ##
* Élaboration de concepts de solutions fonctionnelles à partir des exigences commerciales
* Soutien à la définition des MVP, priorisation du périmètre et élaboration de la feuille de route produit en étroite collaboration avec le Business Owner, le Business Project Manager ainsi que des spécialistes du business et de l-IT
* Traduction des exigences métier en Epics, User Stories et critères d-acceptation, y compris la conduite des sessions de raffinement du backlog
* Élaboration du plan de livraison du projet ainsi que responsabilité du Product Backlog et gestion de l-équipe Scrum
* Préparation et conduite de la planification des sprints, présentation des résultats des sprints et des démonstrations produit, communication transparente envers les parties prenantes et responsabilité du budget du projet

* Diplôme en informatique de gestion ou formation commerciale complétée par une formation continue en gestion de projet
* Expérience de longue date dans la direction, la gestion ou la coordination de projets complexes Business/IT

* Compétences marquées en communication et animation en allemand et en anglais
* Méthode de travail structurée et orientée vers la mise en œuvre avec une grande initiative personnelle
